name: Xray-core
summary: A reusable proxy core that composes inbound protocol listeners, rule or script routing, DNS-aware target strategies, and outbound protocol/transport handlers; its local forwarding core is distinct from any external management service.

features.name: Reusable feature-oriented core
features.description: Xray exposes a reusable core instance whose components are registered and connected through typed feature interfaces. The core processes configured inbound traffic through routing to outbound handlers; it does not by itself define a hosted control plane.
benefits: Supports embedding and composing protocol, DNS, policy, routing, and statistics features
Keeps component contracts explicit while allowing protocol implementations to vary
costs: Component registration and lifecycle ordering create integration constraints
The core still depends on configuration and compatible transport/protocol implementations

features.name: Inbound and outbound protocol/transport boundary
features.description: Inbound workers listen for TCP or UDP traffic, create session metadata, and invoke proxy.Inbound handlers. Outbound handlers instantiate proxy.Outbound implementations, apply target resolution and optional mux/XUDP behavior, then move bytes through the configured transport.
benefits: Separates listener-facing protocol acceptance from egress protocol and transport selection
Supports multiple protocols and transport/security combinations behind common interfaces
costs: DNS target strategies and multiplexing alter session behavior and failure paths
Inbound and outbound configuration must preserve session metadata and destination semantics

features.name: Reloadable rule, balancer, and script routing
features.description: The router evaluates routing context against rules or an optional script, resolves balancers, and atomically publishes rule and balancer maps for route selection. Webhooks observe decisions; they are management/observability hooks rather than a separate forwarding plane.
benefits: Allows route policy changes without rebuilding every protocol handler
Supports rule tags, balancers, DNS-aware matching, scripts, and decision webhooks
costs: Reload and concurrent selection require synchronization and lifecycle cleanup
Route policy can change while long-lived sessions retain already-selected outbound state

mathematical_views.question: How do Xray core features connect inbound listeners, routing, DNS, outbound managers, and transport handlers?
assumptions: Feature interfaces are vertices and construction requirements are edges
The graph is local to one core instance; a remote management service is not inferred
Generated configuration and protocol primitive details are abstracted

mathematical_views.question: How does an accepted connection become an outbound flow with target strategy and optional multiplexing?
assumptions: An inbound worker creates session context and invokes a protocol handler
Routing produces an outbound tag and the outbound handler applies configured target and mux behavior
The model abstracts wire framing and encryption implementation

mathematical_views.question: How can rule and balancer updates become visible to route selection while existing selections remain valid?
assumptions: The router publishes immutable or atomically replaced rule/balancer collections for readers
A route is a decision observation, not a promise that the selected outbound is reachable
The model does not claim zero-delay propagation to every concurrent reader
